title: Jacobi-Zariski sequence for a quotient of a smooth algebra
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $H_1(L_{B/A})=0$ and $\Omega_{B/A}$ is a projective $B$-module (e.g. $A\to B$ smooth) [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], let $\mathfrak a\subseteq B$ be an ideal and $C=B/\mathfrak a$, an $A$-algebra via $A\to B\to C$. Then there is an exact sequence of $C$-modules $$0\to H_1(L_{C/A})\to\mathfrak a/\mathfrak a^2\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }C\otimes_B\Omega_{B/A}\xrightarrow{\ w\ }\Omega_{C/A}\to0,$$ where $\delta(a\bmod\mathfrak a^2)=1\otimes\mathrm da$ and $w(c\otimes\mathrm db)=c\,\mathrm d\bar b$ ($\bar b$ the class of $b$ in $C$; $\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00S2 (lemma-exact-sequence-NL, Jacobi-Zariski sequence, line 35412) for A -> B -> C, including its final assertion (if Tor_1^B(Omega_{B/A},C) = Tor_2^B(Omega_{B/A},C) = 0 then H_1(NL_{B/A} (x)_B C) = H_1(L_{B/A}) (x)_B C), with Lemma Tag 07BP (lemma-NL-surjection, line 35506: H_1(L_{C/B}) = a/a^2, Omega_{C/B} = 0) and Lemma Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq, line 34103) for the maps delta and w; this is the sequence used in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 07M7 ('note that H_1(L_{B/A}) = 0 and that Omega_{B/A} is finite projective, in particular flat so the Tor group vanishes')

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] to A → B → C = B/a. Retain exactness at H1(L_C/A), H1(L_C/B), and C tensor_B Omega_B/A; the left term is the kernel of the base-changed canonical cotangent differential.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-left-term-vanishing]. Tensor symmetry, with LinearMap.rTensor_comm and baseChange_eq_ltensor, carries each element of the left kernel to the zero right-tensor kernel. Thus the left kernel is zero; its map u is zero. Exactness gives injectivity of H1Cotangent.map A B C C.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-surjection-h1], realized by Extension.h1CotangentEquivCotangent on the quotient extension P. Identify P.ker with a using Ideal.mk_ker and transport its cotangent module by cotangentEquivCotangentKer and Ideal.Cotangent.equivOfEq, extending scalars along B → C. Call the resulting C-linear equivalence e. Set i = e composed with H1Cotangent.map, and d = P.cotangentComplex composed with the inverse cotangent identification. Extension.cotangentComplex_comp_h1CotangentEquivCotangent identifies d composed with e with the connecting map. LinearEquiv.conj_exact_iff_exact and surjective precomposition transport the two middle exactness assertions.

Take w = KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange A B C. The differential maps of [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] give surjectivity by mapBaseChange_surjective for the quotient map, the formula for d by Extension.cotangentComplex_mk, and the formula for w by mapBaseChange_tmul and map_D. No use of the final relative differential module is needed.
